# E0202: `without` given twice

A module's header holds one `without`, which names each limit once, as `without panic, alloc`.

- Rule: [`program.header-limits`](../../reference/04-programs.md#program.header-limits)
- Reported at: the second `without` of a header, or the limit named again.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `items` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0202:2
module main
without panic, alloc, panic

pub fn halve(n: i64) -> i64 { n / 2 }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
module main
without panic, alloc

pub fn halve(n: i64) -> i64 { n / 2 }
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0202_limit_given_twice.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0202_limit_given_twice.lt):

```text
── `without` GIVEN TWICE ────────────── E0202_limit_given_twice.lt:2:23  [E0202]

`panic` is already named in this `without`:

  2 │ without panic, alloc, panic
    │                       ^^^^^

A module's header holds one `without`, which names each limit once, as `without
panic, alloc`.

To fix it, delete the repeated `panic`:

  2 │ without panic, alloc, panic
    │                     -------
```

`stilt check` on [`E0202_second_without.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0202_second_without.lt):

```text
── `without` GIVEN TWICE ────────────────── E0202_second_without.lt:3:1  [E0202]

This header already has a `without`:

  3 │ without alloc
    │ ^^^^^^^

A module's header holds one `without`, which names each limit once, as `without
panic, alloc`.

To fix it, name its limits in the first `without`:

  2 │ without panic, alloc
    │              +++++++
  3 │ without alloc
    │ -------------
```
